_why_this_file_exists: R0-C05. Four preparedness projects, capacity for two. XP0 offered the same four as a two-of-four picker with no mechanics behind it: nothing was scheduled, nothing progressed, nothing was displaced and nothing could be verified. This is the state the visual proof (R0-V05, visual bible section 20) describes.
_capacity: Two may be scheduled. That is the whole opportunity cost, and it is enforced in the rules rather than by disabling a button.
_why_conflicts_are_declared_not_scripted: Each project declares the world resources it needs -- a technical team, the mobile reserve cart, the service passage, the clinical bedside group. These are the things R0's world actually holds (src/sim/world.js), not an invented currency. Two scheduled projects that need the SAME resource cannot both have it, so the second to reach it is disrupted. Nothing rolls a die and no pair is special-cased; the collision is a consequence of what the projects require, and `requires` is projected before the participant commits.

_deliberately_deferred: Contention is between SCHEDULED PROJECTS only. The ordinary morning has already committed a technical team to the Underworks and the reserve to the ICU by the time this window opens, and coupling project availability to that live world state would be truer still -- and could make a project unschedulable for reasons the participant cannot yet act on. R0-C06 owns that coupling; the live world state is shown here as context rather than used as a block.
_localisation_owed: Display strings are English literals here because this repository has no locale layer: the reset removed it and R0-I1 did not restore one. `name_key` is kept beside each name as the stable identifier a locale layer will use, so the content does not have to be rewritten when it returns. Arabic and RTL parity are owed and are recorded in the release ledger, not quietly skipped.
